chunks: And Abu Baseer reported from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

You should say while you are at the door of the Masjid: 'In the Name of Allah, and by Allah, and from Allah, and whatever Allah so Desires, and upon the Religion of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the best of the Names are for Allah, and the Praise is for Allah. And, the greetings be upon Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family). The greetings be upon Muhammad son of Abdullah. The greetings be upon you O Prophet, and the Mercy of Allah, and His Blessings.'

The greetings be upon the Prophets of Allah, and His Rasools. The greetings be upon Ibrahim, Friend of the Beneficent. The greetings be upon the Mursil Prophets. The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. The greetings be upon us and upon the righteous servants.

O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and Your Blessings be upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, and be Merciful to Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, just as You Send Favours, and Blessings, and were Merciful upon Ibrahim and the progeny of Ibrahim, You being the Praiseworthy, the Glorious.

O Allah! Send Blessings upon Muhammad and the Progeny of Muhammad, Your servant, and Your Rasool, and upon Ibrahim, Your Friend, and upon Your Prophets and Your Rasools, and Greetings be upon them, and Peace be upon the Mursils. And the Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.

O Allah! Open for me the doors of Your Mercy, and Enable me in Your obedience, and Your Pleasure, and Protect me with protection of the belief forever for as long as You keep me remaining (alive), Majestic being the Praise of Your Face.
The Praise is for Allah Who Made me to be from His delegates, and His visitor, and Made me to be from the ones who build His Masjids, and Made me to be from the ones who whisper to Him.

O Allah! I am Your servant, and Your visitor in Your House, and upon every Host there is a right for the one whom comes to him, and visits him, and You are the best of the Hosts, and the most Honourable visited One.

So I ask You, O Allah, O Beneficent, by You being Allah Who, there is no god for Him. You are Alone, there being no associates for You, and by You being One, Alone, Last, not begetting and not being begotten, and there being no one as a match for Him.
And that Muhammad is Your servant, and Your Rasool. Blessings be upon him and upon the People of his Household. O Generous, O Benevolent, O Glorious, O Compeller, O Benevolent!

I ask You that You should Make Your gift to me due to my visiting You, the first thing You should Give me is to emancipate (liberate) my neck from the Fire. O Allah! Emancipate my neck from the Fire!' - You should be saying three times.
And Expand upon me from Your sustenance, the Permissible, the good, and Turn away from me the evil of Satan among the humans and the Jinns, and evil of the sinful Arabs and non-Arabs'.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when entering the Masjid?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication serves as the prescribed entry ritual (Adab al-Dukhul) for the Sacred Masjid, emphasizing the transition from the mundane to the sacred through specific invocations of Allah's names and greetings upon the Ahl al-Bayt. It structurally moves from praise to a petition for liberation from the Fire, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the spiritual merit of visiting holy sites as a means of drawing closer to God.
